newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA 6-MONTH TEM YIELD FALLS TO 21.89 PCT.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA 6-MONTH TEM YIELD FALLS TO 21.89 PCT.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 78 basis points to 21.89 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 40 billion bolivars of 177- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 22.67 percent coupon for a price of 100.34 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 22.67 percent.

The bank also sold 10 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 23.32 percent coupon at a price of 99.95 percent, and 10 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 23.97 percent coupon at an average price of 99.64 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 110 basis points to 23.39 percent for 269-day bills, and 128 basis points to 24.42 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
